c: Your teacher opens a dashboard and sees that 5 students are having trouble with fractions.
q: What can the teacher do with this information?
o: Give the same homework to everyone
Give extra help to those 5 students
e: Learning Analytics helps teachers understand learning data and make better decisions.

c: An online learning system checks students' answers and automatically selects easier or harder exercises.
e: Automated adaptation is a typical EDM application. The learning system responds to students' performance.

c: Two students get the same test score, but one improves steadily while the other keeps getting worse.
q: Why is looking at their learning history useful?
o: It shows how their learning changes over time
It tells us which student is happier
e: Learning patterns over time provide information that a single score cannot show.

c: On Taiwan's 因材網 platform, a student has difficulty with division. The platform identifies weaker prerequisite knowledge and suggests where to start.
q: Why is this learning path useful?
o: It helps the student work on missing basic skills
e: The 因材網 case illustrates knowledge structures, adaptive diagnosis and prerequisite-based learning paths.

c: A school wants to identify students who may fail a course using their attendance, homework and previous scores.
q: Which method could help the school?
e: Prediction models estimate an outcome from available information. A prediction is not a certainty.

c: Student A opens six hints in 35 seconds and immediately enters the provided answer. This happens repeatedly.
e: Rapidly using hints to obtain answers may indicate gaming the system. However, logs alone cannot prove the student's intentions.

c: Student B completes 22 exercises on one skill. Their accuracy stays around 40%, with no clear improvement.
e: Wheel-spinning describes repeated practice without meaningful progress. The student may need another explanation or different support.

c: Student C quickly opens hints, then spends time thinking and writes an explanation. On the next problem, they answer correctly without hints.
q: Is the quick use of hints always bad?
o: No, the student may be learning from the hints
No, so we should delete all learning logs
e: The student's later explanation and independent success suggest productive learning. The sequence of actions matters.

c: Student D skips a learning video but correctly answers 10 questions in a short time.
o: The student may already know the lesson
e: Skipping content does not automatically mean disengagement. Prior knowledge or advanced ability may explain the behavior.

c: Student E makes two early mistakes, receives one hint and then answers six questions correctly in a row.
e: Improved performance after feedback is useful evidence of learning progress, although it does not prove complete mastery.

c: Two students both spend 30 minutes on an online lesson. One makes progress; the other repeats mistakes.
q: Does more learning time always mean more learning?
o: Yes, if the student clicks many times
No, time alone cannot tell us how much was learned
e: Time on task is only one indicator. Progress, task difficulty and behavior also matter.

c: An AI system labels students as 'not engaged' when they skip videos. However, some advanced students skip videos because the material is too easy.
o: The students use too much technology
The AI may misunderstand their behavior
The videos are always too long
All students should watch more videos
e: A behavior-based label can be misleading. Engagement depends on context, and some groups may be unfairly judged.

c: An AI model is trained mostly on data from typical learners. A twice-exceptional student learns in a different way.
q: What should the school be careful about?
o: The model may not work equally well for every student
Every student must learn in exactly the same way
AI can never be used in education
The student should be excluded from the system
e: Under-represented learners may be misclassified. Schools should check model fairness and avoid assumptions based on limited data.

c: An AI system predicts that a student may fail a course. The prediction is accurate in many previous cases, but the system cannot explain why this particular student was flagged.
o: Ask teachers to review more evidence before taking action
Share the risk label with the whole class
e: Predictions can help identify where support may be needed, but important decisions require human oversight, fairness and privacy safeguards.

c: A school has a large amount of learning data. AI finds patterns, but teachers know the students and understand their learning needs.
q: What is the best way to use this information?
o: Ignore the data and use only test scores
Combine data, learning theory and teacher judgment
e: The central chapter message is that big data does not replace theory. LA, EDM and human interpretation should complement one another.
